name: Bombardier CRJ100/200
summary: 50-seat regional jet developed from the Challenger 600 business jet; still flown in large numbers by SkyWest for United, Delta and American.

wings: Low swept wing with small upturned winglets
Simple wing with no leading-edge slats
engines: Two CF34 turbofans in pods on the rear fuselage, close behind the wing
fuselage: Short, slim 4-abreast tube with a long, pointed nose
tail: Small swept tailplane perched on top of the fin

tellTales: Short, small jet with rear engines and a T-tail
Small winglets on a simple wing
Long pointed nose on a 4-abreast tube

confusedWith.howToTell: The CRJ200 is short and compact with a small slat-less wing; the CRJ700/900 is much longer with a bigger wing, leading-edge slats and larger engines.
The CRJ200 has a fatter 4-abreast body with engines tucked close behind the wing; the ERJ145 is a pencil-thin 3-abreast tube with engines mounted further aft.
The CRJ200 has a much longer fuselage with many more windows and an airline-style door layout; the Challenger is short and stubby with only a few large oval windows.
